sichuan-small-towns-unfinished-resettlem.whole: The project rebuilt roads, water and sewer pipes, canals and river embankments in eight small towns in Sichuan. Twelve of its thirteen objective indicators were met or exceeded by the completion report's count: the number of people with access to the road network reached 30,000 in Puxing Town against a target of 10,250, 20,000 in Panlian against 7,200 and 5,300 in Liujiang against 5,000; travel time along the Luogui Road corridor in Penglai Town fell from 13 minutes to 6; flood protection at Yingxi, Hongchuan and Panlian rose from a 3-to-10-year standard to a 20-year standard; and river water quality at Yingxi and Hongchuan rose from worse than Class V to Class IV. The thirteenth, water supply for 20,000 people in Liujiang Town, was not reached at closing: the treatment plant was 80 per cent built on 31 December 2016 and became fully operational on 30 May 2017. The report's economic rates of return at completion are higher than the appraisal estimate for all eight sub-components costed, 14.49 against 13.71 per cent at Pengshan and 23.02 against 18.50 per cent at Miyi among them, while the net present value fell in two of the eight, from RMB130.20 million to RMB112.84 million at Xinjin and from RMB953.89 million to RMB294.85 million at Miyi. The report records US$17 million of savings and contract prices 30 to 45 per cent below estimate, and the Independent Evaluation Group's review states that the report does not discuss whether the lower prices brought lower-quality materials and works or worse conditions for the workers. Every figure here is the lender's own, from its completion report and the Evaluation Group's review of it; no independent check was found.
sichuan-small-towns-unfinished-resettlem.searched: World Bank completion report of 31 May 2017 (results framework, Annex 2 outputs, Annex 3 economic analysis) and IEG ICR Review ICRR0020788, both read from the cached text on disk.

qufu-gupan-pond-demolition.whole: The loan paid to conserve cultural heritage sites and build tourism facilities at Qufu and Zoucheng. By the completion report's count 40 of the 41 sites were conserved, 18 of 18 in Zoucheng and 22 of 23 in Qufu, the one left out being old mansion No. 10 in the Ming Old City of Qufu, cancelled over unresolved property rights on military land. The report puts direct beneficiaries at 2,349,000 against a target of 2,155,000, non-local tourists at 1,968,000 in Qufu against 1,831,000 and 256,000 in Zoucheng against 217,000, and tourist satisfaction at 96 per cent against a 75 per cent target, that last figure coming from satisfaction surveys run at the Confucius and Mencius complexes under the project. It gives a net present value of US$50 million and an economic rate of return of 16 per cent at completion, where the appraisal document had estimated 27.50 per cent for Qufu, 12.89 per cent for Zoucheng and 8.16 per cent for Nishan; the Evaluation Group's review states that the report does not say how the tourist visits behind that calculation were measured. The completion report's own table splits its Satisfactory outcome rating into Moderately Unsatisfactory before the April 2016 restructuring and Highly Satisfactory after it, and records that the project management company was not hired until 2013, 18 months into implementation. All of these figures come from the Bank's completion report and the Evaluation Group's review of it; no independent check was found.
qufu-gupan-pond-demolition.searched: World Bank completion report of 19 December 2017 (Annex 1 results framework, efficiency section, Table 10) and IEG ICR Review ICRR0021054, read from the cached text on disk.

xiangyang-panggong-resettlement-housing-.whole: The project built 20.04 kilometres of road against a target of 19.92, 17 bus priority intersections, 100 new or upgraded bus stops and 40 new buses, and trained 364 municipal staff against a revised target of 150. Bus speed on the Route 13 corridor reached 19.2 kilometres an hour, meeting a target that had been cut from 24 to 19 at restructuring after the baseline was found to leave out time spent standing at stops. The average annual count of people killed or severely injured in traffic accidents fell to 7 from a baseline of 37, against a target of 25, and 95.1 per cent of a sample of at least 200 public transport users said they were satisfied, against a 90 per cent target; both the baseline and the satisfaction figures come from surveys carried out under the project. The accessibility indicator records 52,000 Panggong residents able to reach the city centre within 30 minutes, a figure the completion report itself calls difficult to assess. The economic rate of return for the urban roads component, 83 per cent of project cost at appraisal, was 14.17 per cent at completion against 17.1 per cent at appraisal, which the completion report attributes to higher costs and a longer construction time; the public transport component, not costed at appraisal, returned 15.53 per cent, and the two together 14.27 per cent. The completion report rated efficiency Modest on those figures and the Independent Evaluation Group's review rated it Substantial. Every figure is the lender's own; no independent check was found.
xiangyang-panggong-resettlement-housing-.searched: World Bank completion report of 31 January 2020 (Annex 1 results framework, Annex 4 efficiency) and IEG ICR Review ICRR0022083, read from the cached text on disk.

nanning-urban-environment-resettlement.whole: The project doubled the Jiangnan wastewater treatment plant from 240,000 to 480,000 cubic metres a day and built five smaller plants with 102,000 cubic metres a day of capacity in Binyang, Hengxian, Manshan, Shanglin and Wuming. Against the original appraisal targets it laid or rehabilitated 56.5 kilometres of primary and secondary sewers where 84.9 were planned, installed 5 of 8 sewage lift stations, and cleaned 10.363 kilometres of river course where 14.245 were planned. Measured against targets rewritten at the September 2015 restructuring, the share of the population with wastewater collection and treatment reached 89.19 per cent against 75.5 per cent, pollution removed came to 10,305 tonnes of biochemical oxygen demand a year against 9,715, and beneficiaries came to 2,955,755 against 2.5 million. The Independent Evaluation Group's review records that the restructuring came three months before the original closing date with about 92 per cent of the loan already spent, that the revised targets were 24 to 80 per cent lower than those agreed at appraisal, and that the completion report states almost none of the treatment plants met the original targets, achieving between 30 and 78 per cent of them. The financial rate of return for the water company was above 6 per cent at appraisal and above 10 per cent at completion. The Evaluation Group rated efficiency Modest, finding the completion report's economic discussion largely carried over from the appraisal document. All these figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.
nanning-urban-environment-resettlement.searched: World Bank completion report of 11 April 2017 (results framework and Annex 3) and IEG ICR Review of 6 September 2017 (outputs, efficacy and efficiency sections), read from the cached text on disk.

liaoning-coastal-zone-resettlement.whole: The project rebuilt streets, water and wastewater works and drainage in coastal and western Liaoning. It delivered 50.70 kilometres of new and rehabilitated street against an original target of 52 kilometres and a target cut to 31.68 at the May 2016 restructuring, 13.65 kilometres of it new road and 37.05 rehabilitated; reclaimed water came to 78 per cent of the water used in the Lingyuan industrial park against an original target of 60 per cent, but only 6 industries were connected to the reclaimed water system where 20 were planned and 5 were the revised target; and direct beneficiaries came to 350,340 against 340,000 planned at appraisal and 213,200 after revision. Satisfaction with the new walking, cycling and bus facilities is reported at 99 and 98 per cent against targets of 70 and 60; the completion report states that all of these figures, including a bus passenger count it reports as 1,218 per cent of target, come from the Provincial Project Management Office, and it calls the reliability of that passenger figure questionable. Economic rates of return at completion were 11.1 per cent at Donggang against 11.9 at appraisal, 18.9 against 17.8 at Kuandian, 19.3 against 14.6 at Lingyuan and 13.9 against 15.3 at Panjin, 14.2 per cent overall. The completion report rated efficiency Substantial and the outcome Satisfactory; the Independent Evaluation Group's review of 26 June 2020 rated efficiency Modest and the outcome Moderately Satisfactory, pointing to four years in which only a third of the loan was spent for want of counterpart money, and to Suizhong and Chaoyang withdrawing from the project. The figures are the lender's and the provincial office's own; no independent check was found.
liaoning-coastal-zone-resettlement.searched: World Bank completion report of 28 March 2020 (Annex 1 results framework, Table 3 economic re-evaluation, Table 4 outcome calculation) and IEG ICR Review ICRR0022097 (efficiency and outcome sections), read from the cached text on disk.

han-river-urban-environment-resettlement.whole: The project built more than 85 kilometres of sewer and three wastewater treatment plants adding 130,000 cubic metres a day of capacity, 3,600 household sewer connections serving about 25,000 people, five sanitary landfills holding 8.29 million cubic metres, five leachate plants treating 660 cubic metres a day, and closed four old dump sites. The share of municipal wastewater treated in the project cities ran from 72 to 95 per cent against a baseline of 0 to 25, and wastewater fee collection from 90 to 96 per cent against about 40 at the start. Against targets, sewer construction fell short in three cities, 23 kilometres at Hanchuan against an original 25 and a revised 35.6, 6.3 at Xiangyang against 12 and 11, and 10 at Shayang against an original 45; solid waste collected and taken to landfill reached 75 per cent at Dawu against an original target of 95 and a revised 90; and 28 industrial polluters installed adequate treatment, a figure the results framework sets against an original target of 36 while the report's text sets it against an original target of 28. The completion report states that no economic or financial rate of return was available and that the benefits of the project were not quantified, that the borrower's contribution came in US$8 million below what was agreed at restructuring, that US$14 million of the loan was cancelled after closing and that actual costs came in about 15 per cent below the revised figure; it rated the overall outcome Moderately Unsatisfactory. Poverty impacts were neither monitored nor measured, by the report's own statement. All the figures are the lender's own, drawn from its completion report and the borrower's section of it; no independent check was found.
han-river-urban-environment-resettlement.searched: World Bank completion report of 15 December 2015 (results framework, sections 3.2 to 3.5, Annex 2 outputs) and IEG ICR Review of 7 November 2016, read from the cached text on disk.

second-shandong-environment-resettlement.whole: The project built 100,000 cubic metres a day of wastewater treatment capacity with 370 kilometres of collection sewers, 105,000 cubic metres a day of water treatment capacity with 432 kilometres of distribution mains, and 780 tonnes a day of landfill capacity across the participating cities and counties. By the completion report's count the share of the population connected to treatment plants reached 90.7 per cent against an 85 per cent target, compliance of connected industries with discharge standards 98.2 per cent against 90, and solid waste coverage 95 per cent, its target. Three indicators fell short or carry the report's own warnings: river water quality improved along 129.5 kilometres against a 148-kilometre target, and the report calls the indicator problematic because no methodology was provided for it; reuse of treated effluent reached 18.2 per cent against 21 per cent, with the report stating that the figure reported by the provincial project office cannot be verified and that its accuracy is questionable; and citizen satisfaction is given as 97 per cent in the results framework and as 93 per cent on average in the report's text, both against a 92 per cent target, from an end-of-project survey run under the project. Under the Global Environment Facility grant, the Yantai septic tank pilot fitted 1,056 tanks against a target of 1,700 and cut discharges to the Bohai Sea by 806.4 tonnes of biochemical oxygen demand a year against a target of 1,700. Rates of return were above 15 per cent at appraisal and the end-of-project analysis concluded that changes during implementation did not significantly affect them; no financial rate of return was calculated. All of these figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.
second-shandong-environment-resettlement.searched: World Bank completion report of 19 June 2014 (results framework, sections 3.2 and 3.3, Annex 2 output tables, Annex 3) and IEG ICR Review ICRR14669, read from the cached text on disk.

shanghai-urban-environment-apl2-resettle.whole: The Western Trunk Sewer carried an average of 377,000 cubic metres a day by closing, 94 per cent of its 400,000 design capacity, against a target of 80 per cent; the Xujing water works served 205,000 people from October 2010 against a target of 200,000; and 12 districts took part in metropolitan environmental measures against a target of 8. Two things were not delivered. The Bailonggang sludge plant treated 178 tonnes a day, 92 per cent of capacity, while the Zhuyuan sludge plant, phase one of 150 tonnes a day, was built by November 2013 but never tested and is recorded at zero. The solid waste component was dropped at the March 2014 restructuring with the two dump sites it was to close still open, the borrower agreeing to close them with its own money by June 2016; 10 institutional strengthening activities were completed against a revised target of 11 and 15 identified at appraisal. No cost-benefit analysis was done either at appraisal or at completion. The Independent Evaluation Group's review records a four-year delay, total project cost rising 29 per cent from US$434.24 million to US$559.84 million, counterpart funding rising 53 per cent from US$254 million to US$388 million, and price rises of 86 per cent for water supply and 89 per cent for wastewater that still did not bring cost recovery to the level the loan covenants required; it rated efficiency Modest and the three sub-objectives Substantial, Modest and Negligible. The figures all come from the lender's completion report and the Evaluation Group's review of it; no independent check was found.
shanghai-urban-environment-apl2-resettle.searched: World Bank completion report of 30 November 2015 (results framework, Annex 2) and IEG ICR Review ICRR0020084 (efficiency and outcome sections), read from the cached text on disk.

liuzhou-environment-management-resettlem.whole: By the completion report's count the city was collecting and treating 475,000 cubic metres of wastewater a day at closing, its target, from a baseline of 60,000, with 500,000 cubic metres a day of capacity built, and water quality in the Liujiang River downstream of the city was held at Class III. Two parts of the programme were cut back after objections from the public: 42 of 62 planned public toilets were built, with 20 cancelled, alongside 30 portable and 2 mobile toilets, and all 42 planned community solid waste collection stations were cancelled, leaving only the 450 tonne a day transfer station. Industrial pollution loads fell by 9,668 tonnes of chemical oxygen demand a year against a target of 10,428, with two of the 11 targeted polluters going bankrupt, and the report states that reductions in heavy metals could not be measured. Citizen satisfaction with sanitary conditions rose from 78 per cent in 2007 to 84 per cent in late 2010, with no survey taken at closing. The economic rate of return was 9.5 per cent at appraisal, covering 81 per cent of project cost, and was not recalculated at closing; the Independent Evaluation Group's review rated efficiency modest for want of that analysis and lowered the outcome to Moderately Satisfactory. All the figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.
liuzhou-environment-management-resettlem.searched: World Bank completion report of 13 February 2012 (results framework, Annex 2) and IEG ICR Review of 17 December 2012 (efficiency and outcome sections), read from the cached text on disk.

zhanghu-railway-resettlement.whole: The line is 286 kilometres of double-track, electrified, passenger-only railway, and it opened a month before the COVID-19 pandemic. Journey time between Zhangjiakou and Hohhot fell from 411 minutes to 86 against a target of 100. Traffic came in below target: 21 train pairs a day at closing against 25, reaching 25 by the end of 2020, and annualised ridership of 4 million against a target of 9 million, with 6.4 million for the whole of 2020. The completion report puts the final cost at RMB31.2 billion, 10 per cent below the RMB34.65 billion feasibility estimate, and the cost per kilometre at RMB83 million against RMB93 million and RMB85 million on two comparable Bank-financed lines. Its main text gives an ex-post economic rate of return of 8.4 per cent while its own Annex 4 and the Independent Evaluation Group's review give 8 per cent, against 15 per cent at appraisal, which had counted freight and wider economic benefits that did not materialise; the net present value at completion is minus RMB18.4 billion, about minus US$3.0 billion, against plus RMB6.0 billion at appraisal. The Evaluation Group records that three of the four Bank-financed high-speed lines in China returned 15, 16 and 18 per cent. All of these figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.
zhanghu-railway-resettlement.searched: World Bank completion report of 30 June 2021 (Annex 1 results framework, paragraphs 28 to 30, Annex 4 economic analysis) and IEG ICR Review ICRR0022658 (efficiency section), read from the cached text on disk.

luan-huaibei-urban-transport-resettlemen.whole: Across the four cities the project reports bus ridership on the improved corridors of 634,838 passengers a day against a target of 571,316, annual urban bus ridership of 366.2 million against 348.6 million, and 42 people killed or injured on the corridors against a target of 261. The two cities where land was taken for this case did worse than the others. In Huaibei the Huaihai Road rehabilitation and the Tuohe bus maintenance depot were both cancelled, 146 of 248 planned off-street bus parking spaces were provided, corridor bus ridership came to 122,500 a day against a target of 132,000, and annual urban bus ridership came to 69.55 million against 79.02 million; the completion report attributes both shortfalls to that cancellation and to the city's car ownership growing fastest of the four. Bus travel time between selected points averaged 188 minutes against a target of 185, with Anqing rising to 23 minutes from a 20-minute baseline against a 19-minute target and Lu'an missing its target by one minute, which the report attributes to rising car ownership. The economic rate of return for the whole project was 23.5 per cent at completion against 17.2 per cent at appraisal, while the net present value fell from US$203.1 million at appraisal to US$143.7 million at completion; US$22.36 million, 22.36 per cent of the loan, was cancelled at closing. Every figure is the lender's own; no independent check was found.
luan-huaibei-urban-transport-resettlemen.searched: World Bank completion report of 28 December 2018 (Annex 1 results framework, paragraphs 30 to 31 and Table 3, efficiency discussion by city) and IEG ICR Review ICRR0021546, read from the cached text on disk.

zhegan-line-railway-resettlement.whole: Annex 2 of the completion report sets the works against the appraisal plan: 1,164 kilometres of track realigned and upgraded against about 900 planned, signalling and communications improved over 939 kilometres against 916 route kilometres, 2,826 of 3,045 planned track kilometres electrified, 23 of 28 track maintenance machines bought, and depot coverage extended to 73,000 track kilometres against a target of 67,000 from a baseline of 40,000. The four planned technical assistance studies were not carried out, the money being moved to buying more track equipment. Transit times per trip fell from 1,575 to 931 minutes for freight trains against a target of 1,400, from 829 to 561 minutes for passenger trains against 600 and from 660 to 336 minutes for express trains; average track downtime halved from 180 to 90 minutes a day; freight traffic reached 51.6 billion tonne-kilometres against a target of 42.6 billion and passenger traffic 40.1 billion passenger-kilometres against 27.3 billion. The completion report puts the economic rate of return at 26 per cent at completion against 19 per cent in the appraisal document, with a net present value of RMB33 billion, and attributes the improvement to passenger traffic growing nearly 50 per cent between 2003 and 2007; the Independent Evaluation Group's review repeats the 19 and 26 per cent figures in its text but prints 23 per cent as the appraisal rate in its own table. No return was recalculated for the track machinery component, estimated at 106 per cent at appraisal. All the figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.
zhegan-line-railway-resettlement.searched: World Bank completion report of 15 August 2008 (results framework, Annex 2 outputs, Annex 3 economic analysis) and IEG ICR Review ICRR13032 (efficiency section and its rate table), read from the cached text on disk.

nanchang-line-2-demolition.whole: The loan helped build all 23.8 kilometres of metro Line 2 and its 21 underground stations, with rolling stock and operating systems; stage one opened on 18 August 2017 and stage two on 30 June 2019, a year later than planned. Weekday ridership reached 206,800 passenger trips by October 2019 against a target of 200,000, having averaged 189,500 a day when the line fully opened in June 2019, and 91 per cent of users rated the service satisfactory against a target of 70 per cent. The travel-time indicator averaged 23 minutes saved against a target of 22, made up of 25 minutes saved between the high-speed rail station and Nanchang railway station, which met its target, 27 minutes between Xinjia'an and Wolongshan against a 25-minute target and 17 minutes between the high-speed rail station and Metro Mansion against 15. Two of those three segments therefore fell short while the average met its mark. The share of Line 2 commuters with a car available reached 40 per cent against a target of 15. The project cost about 15 per cent less than estimated at appraisal, and the economic rate of return was 11.93 per cent at completion against 9.6 per cent at appraisal, with a net present value of RMB8.00 billion and a benefit-cost ratio of 1.6 against 1.2. Every figure is the lender's own; no independent check was found.
nanchang-line-2-demolition.searched: World Bank completion report of 31 December 2019 (Annex 1 results framework, paragraphs 32 to 34, Annex 4) and IEG ICR Review ICRR0022446 (efficiency section), read from the cached text on disk.

henan-towns-water-land-acquisition.whole: The loan was to build water supply and wastewater services in county towns across Henan. By the completion report's count 2.17 million people gained access to improved water supply, against an original target of 4.20 million and a target cut to 2.36 million at the November 2012 restructuring, and 697,000 gained wastewater services, against an original 811,000 and a revised 563,000; both counts cover only the 20 counties still in the project at the end of 2012. The participating utilities' aggregate net profit after tax was minus RMB5.58 million against an original target of plus RMB110.4 million and a revised plus RMB69.34 million, and the report states that even that figure does not reflect the utilities' true position because most remain government-controlled and subsidised. Subprojects in 17 counties were dropped: eleven, about a third of the loan, after their retroactive procurement documents were all found ineligible for Bank financing, and six that found other money; planned costs fell from US$302.62 million to US$239.27 million. Economic rates of return at completion were 21.9 per cent for the low-income counties sampled, 12.5 for the middle-income county and 31.1 for the high-income counties, against 25.8, 25.0 and 33.6 per cent at appraisal, and financial rates of return for the water components ran from 0 to 12.4 per cent against 9.6 to 16.4 per cent at appraisal, which the report attributes to tariffs well below appraisal assumptions, utilities employing more staff than needed and unaccounted-for water still running at 30 to 60 per cent. The completion report rated the overall outcome Unsatisfactory, and the development objective had been rated Unsatisfactory in every implementation report from June 2010 onwards. All the figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.
henan-towns-water-land-acquisition.searched: World Bank completion report of 24 December 2013 (results framework, sections 1.7, 2.2, 3.3 and 3.4, Annex 3) and IEG ICR Review of 17 October 2014, read from the cached text on disk.

sichuan-wudu-canal-resettlement.whole: By the completion report's count the project finished the 108-kilometre Xizi main canal, 305.24 kilometres of sub-main and branch canals, 38.91 kilometres of lateral canals in the demonstration areas and 22 operation and maintenance plans, each exactly at its target, and brought 929,600 mu, about 620 square kilometres, into the irrigation command area while adding 137.5 million cubic metres a year of industrial and domestic water supply capacity. All of those targets were set at the December 2017 restructuring; the original targets in the results framework were nil. The report records 1.2 million farmers as benefiting against a target of 1.1515 million, but its own comment ties the water actually reaching farmland to on-farm works that start after the loan closed and that the Bank did not finance: 11 of 52 lateral canals in the wider scheme and 3 of 9 water treatment plants were under construction at the last field visit in September 2020. The economic rate of return was 11 per cent at completion against 13 per cent at appraisal, which the report attributes to those on-farm works beginning after closure rather than before, and a sensitivity test gives 6 per cent if the local governments' on-farm investment slips beyond 2025. Project costs came to 96 per cent of the appraisal estimate and the loan was fully drawn. Every figure is the lender's own; no independent check was found.
sichuan-wudu-canal-resettlement.searched: World Bank completion report of 19 November 2020 (Annex 1 results framework, paragraphs 43 to 54, Annex 4 rate of return calculation) and IEG ICR Review ICRR0022453 (efficacy and efficiency sections), read from the cached text on disk.

yining-urban-roads-demolition.whole: The project improved 30.4 kilometres of road in central Yining and built 33.54 kilometres in the new development area, after 8.5 kilometres of planned new road was dropped because it no longer fitted the city's master plan and land was hard to obtain; two bus terminals and two fuel stations were also cancelled and four existing terminals upgraded instead, and a planned study of the road maintenance system was not carried out. It installed 33 sets of traffic signals and 88 traffic cameras, and bought 250 cleaner buses while 216 old ones were retired, taking the fleet from 329 in 2012 to 497 in 2017 and the share of residents living within 300 metres of a bus stop from 33 to 60 per cent. Annual bus ridership rose from 77 million to 105.5 million trips against a target of 96 million; morning peak travel time on the two improved corridors fell 10 per cent, its target; 61,000 people in the new area gained access to urban transport against a target of 60,000; and the completion report records no road deaths in the three years after the works against 2.6 deaths per 10,000 motor vehicles before them. The economic rate of return was 14.2 per cent at completion covering 88 per cent of project cost, where the appraisal estimate of 9 per cent covered only the urban roads component, 28 per cent of cost. All of these figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.
yining-urban-roads-demolition.searched: World Bank completion report of 25 June 2018 (paragraphs 11 to 23, Table 2 cost-benefit summary, Annex 1 results framework) and IEG ICR Review ICRR0021326, read from the cached text on disk.

shaying-river-sanba-village-resettlement.whole: Every physical target in the completion report's results framework was met: 206 navigation structures and 206 navigation aids installed, four bridges rebuilt, two ship locks constructed and 585 training programmes run against a target of 550. Traffic went well past target. The share of vessels of 500 deadweight tonnes and over passing the locks reached 97 per cent at Genglou against a target of 25, 99 per cent at Fuyang against a revised 34 and 99 per cent at Yingshang against a revised 99; cargo through Genglou lock reached 13 million tonnes a year against a revised target of 3.6 million and through Fuyang 11.9 million against 3.0 million. The economic rate of return was 31.5 per cent at completion against 14.6 per cent at appraisal, and 21.6 per cent under the report's conservative case of costs 20 per cent higher and benefits 20 per cent lower. The report also records that the Bank declared misprocurement on two contracts in June 2014, over the conflict of interest clause in the bidding documents, without cancelling any of the loan, and that land acquisition by the county land bureaus was delayed. All the figures come from the Bank's completion report and the Independent Evaluation Group's review of it; no independent check was found.
shaying-river-sanba-village-resettlement.searched: World Bank completion report ICR00004372 of 18 June 2018 (Annex 1 results framework including intermediate indicators, paragraphs 31 to 33, Annex 4) and IEG ICR Review ICRR0021305, read from the cached text on disk.

tongliang-road-land-lease-compensation.whole: Across the districts and counties the project built or rehabilitated 77.6 kilometres of road, against an original target of 100 kilometres and a revised target of 77.6, and in Tongliang itself three roads totalling 31.5 kilometres where five rural roads of 25.6 kilometres were planned. By the completion report's count 341,000 people gained road access against an original target of 306,000 and a revised 230,000; 24,340 people completed vocational training against a target of 13,000; 822 standardised community health facilities were put into operation against a revised target of 727; and 822,000 people gained primary health care at community level against a target of 336,000. Direct beneficiaries came to 6,672,860 against a revised target of 8,582,570, which the report attributes to the Yubei District Central Hospital being still under construction at closing. The water supply component was dropped at the first restructuring and the schemes were built without Bank money at 17,500 cubic metres a day against the 12,800 originally planned. The Tongliang road returned 16.7 per cent at completion against 18.23 per cent at appraisal, with the net present value falling from RMB182.0 million to RMB82.6 million, and the Yongchuan road 9.2 per cent against 15.9 per cent with the net present value falling from RMB106.4 million to RMB10.6 million; the training components returned 18.42 per cent at Wushan, 20.7 at Yubei and 14.1 at the Chongqing Technology and Business University but 1.3 per cent at Shizhu, and the report found that fees at the sampled rural clinics did not cover their investment, maintenance and running costs. Every figure is the lender's own; no independent check was found.
tongliang-road-land-lease-compensation.searched: World Bank completion report ICR00004173 of 8 February 2018 (Annex 1 results framework, drinking water and efficiency sections, Annex 4 including Table A4-1) and IEG ICR Review ICRR0021166 (outputs list), read from the cached text on disk.

guangxi-poor-rural-land-acquisition.whole: In the Guangxi counties the completion report records the share of households below the poverty line set by the 2004 participatory assessment falling from 80.8 to 31.2 per cent, households taking part in project planning rising from 13.6 to 86.9 per cent against a target of 80, villagers benefiting from rural infrastructure rising from 6.3 to 92.2 per cent against a target of 80, women taking part in project activities from 2.8 to 59.1 per cent against a target of 30, and the number of girls dropping out of school falling from three to none. Three Guangxi indicators fell short of their targets of 100 per cent: 78.6 per cent of households received project assistance, 70.7 per cent received training and 76.8 per cent received the relevant basic education support. Annual surveys of 1,800 project and non-project households by China's National Statistics Bureau, paid for by the project and by separate British aid grants, put net income a head in Guangxi project villages at RMB1,983 in 2006 and RMB3,217 in 2010, a rise of 38.7 per cent, which the report describes as similar to the provincial average, against rises of 58.5 per cent in Sichuan and 83.3 per cent in Yunnan, the last of these 11.2 points above its provincial average; the share of Guangxi project households with running water rose from about 23 per cent in 2007 to 47 per cent in 2010. The economic rate of return for the project as a whole was 30 per cent at completion, the same as at appraisal, with 31 per cent for mountain agriculture against 35 at appraisal, 29 per cent for rural infrastructure against 27 and 22 per cent for basic education against 19. The surveys behind these figures were commissioned under the project, so the figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.
guangxi-poor-rural-land-acquisition.searched: World Bank completion report ICR1835 of 20 December 2011 (results framework for Guangxi, sections 2.3, 3.2 and 3.3, Annex 5 monitoring results tables) and IEG ICR Review of 27 January 2014, read from the cached text on disk.

rogun-stage1-resettlement.whole: The credit and grants paid for meters and for two assessment studies, not for building the dam. By the completion report's count 215,835 electricity meters were delivered against a revised target of 215,000, of which 171,904, about 80 per cent, were installed, and 143,790 gas meters were delivered against a target cut from 160,000 to 144,000, about 93,000 of them paid for by the Bank; the two Rogun studies, a techno-economic assessment and an environmental and social assessment, were finished in August 2014 against a date of December 2013. The loss reduction targets were missed. Unaccounted-for electricity in the Dushanbe system stood at 17.5 per cent at completion against a revised target of 14.5 per cent and a 2004 baseline of 13 per cent, which the report attributes to the system being overloaded in winter after gas imports from Uzbekistan stopped in 2012; cash collections were 84.7 per cent of billed consumption against 89 per cent; the Dushanbe tariff reached 2.04 US cents a kilowatt-hour against a target of 2.40; billed electricity sales reached 2,236 gigawatt-hours against a target of 1,940; and the gas indicators could not be measured after 2012. The Independent Evaluation Group's assessment of 2020 reports unaccounted-for electricity at 15.3 per cent in 2019, up from 14.5 per cent in 2011, the tariff at 1.89 cents against a target of 2.45, net losses at the power utility Barqi Tojik almost doubling from 1.72 to 3.31 billion somoni by 2018 and its net equity falling from minus 2.75 to minus 9.09 billion somoni; it records that the studies helped the government raise Eurobond finance and that two of Rogun's six planned turbines were commissioned by September 2019. All these figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.
rogun-stage1-resettlement.searched: World Bank completion report ICR3310 of 29 June 2015 (results framework, sections 1.6 and 1.7), IEG ICR Review ICRR14942 and IEG Project Performance Assessment Report of 2020 (overview findings on losses, tariffs and utility finances), read from the cached text on disk.

kwabenya-landfill-expropriation.whole: The Kwabenya landfill, with base costs put at US$9.5 million, was dropped from the credit at the October 2010 mid-term review, along with about US$4 million for private landfill operators and the road to the Tema septage plant. What the credit did deliver, by the Bank's own count, was 16.8 kilometres of primary and secondary storm drain rebuilt and lined in Accra, Kumasi, Sekondi-Takoradi and Tema, as planned and at US$863,000 a kilometre against US$1 million estimated at appraisal; latrines reaching 189,463 people against a target of 230,000 and 49,420 school pupils against 70,000, 80 per cent of the combined target, with household latrines costing US$25 a head, about 50 per cent more than at appraisal; an increase of at least 5 per cent a year in solid waste collected in all five project towns, the target; and small roads, side drains, water and street lighting in 14 low-income communities serving about 100,000 people, against 13 communities and 80,800 people planned. The project's single objective indicator, a fall in the number of residents complaining about refuse and flooding, was never measured directly: the completion report infers a 38.8 per cent reduction from before-and-after answers about household collection and skip access in a beneficiary assessment, and treats anecdotal evidence of less flooding as meeting the 50 per cent target. The Independent Evaluation Group's field assessment of 2016 found solid waste in most of the drains it visited and silt and plant growth in the primary drains, and reports that 47 per cent of beneficiary assessment respondents said their health had improved. All these figures come from the lender's own documents; no independent check was found.
kwabenya-landfill-expropriation.searched: World Bank completion report of 27 June 2013 (results framework and its footnotes), IEG ICR Review ICRR14631 and IEG Project Performance Assessment Report of 2016 (outputs, outcomes and efficiency paragraphs 2.32 to 2.64, Appendix E), read from the cached text on disk.

santa-fe-road-19-expropriation.whole: The loan turned 130 kilometres of National Road 19 in Santa Fe into a four-lane highway, with grade-separated interchanges and overpasses, and the road opened to traffic in 2012. Travel times fell by 8 to 23 per cent on every segment measured, against a target of at least 5 per cent, and road deaths on the road fell 73.3 per cent between 2007 and 2012 while deaths province-wide rose 13.6 per cent; the follow-up safety data came from the Provincial Road Safety Agency, set up in 2010, where the baseline had come from a different body, and the traffic counts behind the travel-time figures were taken in October and November 2012, after the loan closed, by the University of Cordoba working under the project's management unit. The economic rate of return was 12.4 per cent at completion against 19.3 per cent at appraisal, where the appraisal had also given a net present value of US$67.1 million; the completion report and the Independent Evaluation Group's review attribute the fall to the works being let as five segments rather than the three the appraisal costed, to the exclusion of the 2.4-kilometre Santo Tome urban extension, and to the use of the national roads authority's traffic counts in place of the appraisal's rough estimates, which had assumed traffic growth from the first year when there was none during construction. The road safety pilot works were completed only at closing with no before-and-after results analysed, and of the institutional activities most began late and one was finished by closing. Every figure is the lender's own; no independent check was found.
santa-fe-road-19-expropriation.searched: World Bank completion report of 24 June 2013 (results framework, sections 2.3, 3.2 and 3.3) and IEG ICR Review (efficiency section and its rate table), read from the cached text on disk.

sutp-brts-corridor-displacement.whole: The loan and grant paid for bus rapid transit in three cities and traffic systems in others. Pimpri-Chinchwad's four corridors run 48.3 kilometres: by the completion report's count daily ridership on Corridor 2 rose from 67,791 at its launch in October 2015 to 82,100 by December 2016, and on Corridor 3 from 10,566 at its launch in December 2015 to 21,108 by February 2018, while Corridor 1 opened only in August 2018 and Corridor 4 just before closing. Hubli-Dharwad's 22.25-kilometre line was still in trial running at closing, carrying about 55,000 passengers a day. Public transport's share of trips reached 8.82 per cent in Pimpri-Chinchwad against a target of 8 from a baseline of 4.2, and 42.4 per cent between Raipur and Naya Raipur against a revised target of 40 and an original 50; the Hubli-Dharwad mode share indicator is recorded as 0 and not yet measured. Sixteen sustainable transport practices were taken up by cities against a target of six, and forecast carbon dioxide savings came to 312,000 tonnes over ten years against 128,000. The economic rate of return for the three demonstration projects together was 11.2 per cent at closing with a net present value of US$276 million, against 24 per cent and US$185 million estimated at appraisal for two Pimpri-Chinchwad corridors and 29.5 per cent and US$448 million estimated for Hubli-Dharwad at design stage; the report attributes the fall to costs rising about 15 per cent in rupees and to benefits starting late because two of the systems had only just opened. All the figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.
sutp-brts-corridor-displacement.searched: World Bank completion report of 25 March 2019 (Annex 1 results framework, paragraph 27 economic analysis, city annexes for Pimpri-Chinchwad, Naya Raipur and Hubli-Dharwad) and IEG ICR Review ICRR0021663 (efficiency section), read from the cached text on disk.

dar-brt-kariakoo-clearance.whole: The bus rapid transit works were finished by December 2015, 100 per cent complete by value, and interim operations began on 10 May 2016. Rush-hour travel time between Ubungo and the central business district fell from 62 to 28 minutes against a target of 25. The service ran well below plan: 140 buses were operating at closing against a revised target of 248 and an original 305, and public transport passengers through Jangwani came to 162,000 a day against a target of 360,000 and a baseline of 250,000, with an estimated 200,000 more carried by daladalas on the parallel route; users along the corridor rated the service Moderately Satisfactory against a Satisfactory target, being least satisfied with waiting times. The airport side of the project finished the Zanzibar runway rehabilitation in August 2010, ahead of schedule, and the airport met the target of a satisfactory rating from airlines and passengers in a survey. The cost of the bus rapid transit roadworks rose 70 per cent from US$110 million to US$177 million between appraisal and the 2012 restructuring, and the completion report's ex-post economic rate of return, worked out at the actual average ridership of 125,809 a day, is 1.8 per cent, against 14.5 per cent at appraisal and 12.4 per cent at restructuring; the same model gives 8.4 per cent at 250,000 riders a day and 18 per cent at the 524,000 planned. All of these figures come from the lender's own completion report and the Independent Evaluation Group's review of it; no independent check was found.
dar-brt-kariakoo-clearance.searched: World Bank completion report of 7 November 2017 (results framework, section 3.3 efficiency paragraphs 45 to 48) and IEG ICR Review, read from the cached text on disk.

nutrip-road-compensation-arrears.whole: Little of the road programme was built. By the completion report's count 20 kilometres of road were rehabilitated, part of the Meru bypass, against a target of 118 kilometres, and US$61.87 million of the US$300 million credit was spent. Travel time from the James Gichuru junction to Rironi stayed at three hours against a target of 2.1 hours and vehicle operating costs stayed at US$1.50 a kilometre against a target of US$1.10, in both cases because the works were still unfinished; the road crash indicator fell 22 per cent in 2017 against a target of 15 per cent, which the report credits to enforcement by the National Transport Safety Authority rather than to the works; the indicator on private sector participation was not achieved. Costs of what was being built rose steeply: civil works on the James Gichuru to Rironi section from US$54.08 million at appraisal to US$163.8 million, the Kisumu bypass from US$8.45 million to US$41.77 million and the Meru bypass from US$25.0 million to US$34.4 million, while the resettlement plan for James Gichuru to Rironi rose from US$1.3 million to US$120 million. The Meru bypass returned 30.7 per cent ex-post against 17.2 per cent at appraisal, with a net present value of US$91.19 million against US$11.6 million; no return was worked out for the James Gichuru to Rironi section, which was 18 per cent physically complete at the completion mission. The completion report and the Independent Evaluation Group's review both rated the outcome Unsatisfactory and efficacy Negligible. Every figure is the lender's own; no independent check was found.
nutrip-road-compensation-arrears.searched: World Bank completion report of 26 June 2019 (Annex 1 results framework, paragraphs 25 to 31 with Tables 3 and 4, Annex 4 Table 4.8) and IEG ICR Review (efficacy and efficiency sections), read from the cached text on disk.

bukoba-airport-resettlement-arrears.whole: The project rehabilitated or maintained 909 kilometres of road, 268 kilometres under the roads component and 641 kilometres with 212 culverts and two bridges under emergency maintenance in 19 of Tanzania's 31 regions, about 14 per cent of the national paved network, and rebuilt four airports. Vehicle operating costs fell from US$0.34 to US$0.22 a kilometre on the Korogwe-Same road against a target of US$0.23 and from US$0.45 to US$0.27 on Arusha-Minjingu against US$0.25; the share of classified roads in good or fair condition is given as 86 per cent against a target of 70, with the completion report stating that inconsistency in how the indicator was measured makes the achievement difficult to assess. At Bukoba the runway was extended and paved, a new terminal built after the old one was condemned following an earthquake, and the airport rated able to take ATR-42 aircraft; its traffic reached 33,138 passengers in 2016 against a target of 34,000, and the average number of passengers per aircraft rose from 8.6 in 2009 to 18.6 in 2017. Of the other three airports Zanzibar carried 946,905 passengers against a target of 660,000, Kigoma 29,781 against 40,000 and Tabora 16,505 against 30,000, below its baseline of 22,912, which the report attributes to restrictions on operations during the extended works. Ex-post economic rates of return were 18.3 per cent at Bukoba against 15 per cent at appraisal, 8.5 per cent at Kigoma against 23 per cent and minus 9.6 per cent at Tabora, and 17.1 per cent on the Korogwe-Same road against 19 and 19.9 per cent at appraisal and 16.3 per cent on Arusha-Minjingu against 15.2; the report rated efficiency Modest. All these figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.
bukoba-airport-resettlement-arrears.searched: World Bank completion report of 16 January 2017 (Annex 1 results framework, paragraphs 28 to 43 including the efficiency assessment, airport-by-airport discussion) and IEG ICR Review, read from the cached text on disk.
